question.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2=4.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R (y-z)\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2} \:\textrm{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \, \mathrm{d}V = 
\iiint\limits_{\Delta} \, f(\rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \rho\cos\phi) \:  \rho^2\sin\phi \: \mathrm{d}\rho \, \mathrm{d}\theta \, \mathrm{d}\phi.
$$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
z = \rho\cos\phi
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
\Delta = \left\{ (\rho, \theta, \phi) \, : \, 0 \leq \rho \leq 2, \: 0 \leq \theta \lt 2\pi, \: 0 \leq \phi \leq \pi \right\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=(y-z)\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(y-z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
